gs_scope: Caller and person overdosing are immune from simple-possession charges; civil immunity for administering naloxone. No training required.
how_to_get_quickly: Pharmacy (no Rx) or a Regional Overdose Prevention Specialist (ROPS).
barriers: Rural access; NEXT Distro mail is paused until 7/31/26. Use ROPS or a pharmacy.

gs_scope: Weak: a defense (not immunity) for the first caller on small possession, and it cannot be reused within 18 months. Administering naloxone is separately shielded.
how_to_get_quickly: More Narcan Please shut down Feb 2024. Free mail + 10 regional hubs now at Naloxone Texas (naloxonetexas.com), or pharmacy standing order.

naloxone_legal_status: Legal — Naloxone and other opioid antagonists may be prescribed, dispensed, possessed, and administered under state law and a statewide standing order.
gs_scope: Limited — Affirmative defense for certain possession/paraphernalia charges when someone reports an overdose, stays, and cooperates; not blanket immunity from arrest or all charges.
pharmacy_mechanism: Statewide standing order plus OTC — Pharmacists can dispense under the standing order, and Narcan and similar products are also sold OTC.
medicaid_notes: Covered — All forms of opioid antagonists under the standing order are covered by Medicaid without prior authorization for Medicaid patients of record.
how_to_get_quickly: Pharmacy (standing order or OTC) or free kits from sites listed on Stop the Opidemic and UtahNaloxone.org (health departments, libraries, community partners)
barriers: Rural pharmacy access; out‑of‑pocket cost for uninsured people; variable pharmacy stocking; confusion about legal protections and OTC vs prescription routes.

gs_scope: HB 2117 (2025): good-faith callers and helpers cannot be arrested or prosecuted for personal-use possession, or jailed for a related probation/parole violation. Excludes distribution, felon-in-possession, outstanding warrants.
how_to_get_quickly: REVIVE! free training + naloxone via local health depts and CSBs: https://dbhds.virginia.gov/behavioral-health/substance-abuse-services/revive/ — or pharmacy, or https://nextdistro.org/virginia
barriers: Rural SW VA has dedicated programs.

gs_scope: 18 V.S.A. 4254: caller and victim protected from arrest and prosecution for drug possession and related violations.
how_to_get_quickly: Free naloxone via UVM Community First Responder program (short online training), a pharmacy, or a district health office.

gs_scope: RCW 69.50.315: caller and victim protected from simple-possession prosecution; not distribution, and evidence stays usable for other charges.
how_to_get_quickly: Free naloxone by mail from People's Harm Reduction Alliance (phra.org/naloxone), a pharmacy (no Rx), or find a site at stopoverdose.org.

gs_scope: Caller who stays and IDs themselves is immune from minor possession, underage-drinking, and public-intox charges. The overdose victim gets the same but must complete a court-approved treatment program.
SF0074 (2025): last state to adopt immunity. Good-faith callers who stay are protected, up to 2 incidents per 12 months (2nd requires agreeing to treatment).
how_to_get_quickly: NEW (May 2026): WDH Community Naloxone Resource Map — free Narcan at 30 sites in 22 of 23 counties: https://health.wyo.gov/publichealth/prevention/substanceabuseandsuicide/opioid-information-wyoming/opioid-overdose-response/ — or pharmacy.
